meta.title: Long-Read & RNA-seq Isoform Knowledge Explorer
meta.description: Interactive knowledge maps for long-read and RNA-seq isoform analysis software and methods.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq Nanopore long-read data
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Multiple specialized computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed, with diverse strategies. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We evaluated ten state-of-the-art methods, spanning four analytical dimensions: barcodes and UMI detection, demultiplexing and UMI clustering, gene-level expression profiling, and isoform detection and quantification. Using real and simulated datasets across different protocols, sequencing depths and chemistries, we assessed the accuracy, robustness, and scalability of each tool. Our results revealed method-specific trade-offs, and highlight the importance of sequencing quality and UMI correction strategies. This benchmark provides a practical resource for optimizing isoform analysis and accurate gene expression profiling in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics using long-read sequencing. Our benchmarking workflow is designed to be reusable, thereby enabling method developers to compare their own approaches against the set of reference methods evaluated in this work.

papers.title: Benchmarking long-read RNA-sequencing technologies with LongBench: a cross-platform reference dataset profiling cancer cell lines with bulk and single-cell approaches
papers.abstract: Long-read RNA sequencing enables full-length transcript profiling and improved isoform resolution, but variable platforms and evolving chemistries demand careful benchmarking for reliable application. We present LongBench, a matched, multi-platform reference dataset spanning bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus transcriptomics across eight human lung cancer cell lines with synthetic spike-in controls. LongBench incorporates three state-of-the-art long-read protocols alongside Illumina short reads: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PCR-cDNA, ONT direct RNA, and PacBio Kinnex. We systematically evaluate transcript capture, quantification accuracy, differential expression, isoform usage, variant detection, and allele-specific analyses. Our results show high concordance in gene-level differential analyses across protocols, but reduced consistency for transcript-level and isoform analyses due to length- and platform-dependent biases. Single-cell long-read data are highly concordant with bulk for high-confidence features, though single-nuclei data show reduced feature detection. LongBench provides one of the largest publicly available longread benchmarking resources, enabling rigorous cross-platform evaluation and guiding technology selection for transcriptomic research.

papers.title: Comparison of single-cell long-read and short-read transcriptome sequencing via cDNA molecule matching: quality evaluation of the MAS-ISO-seq approach
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing is used for profiling gene expression differences between cells. It can be performed with short reads, which provide high-throughput and high-quality information at the gene level, or with long reads, which provide isoform resolution via preserving full-length transcripts. It is, however, unclear how comparable the data is between the two methods. We investigate the types of bias introduced at the library preparation and the bioinformatic processing steps on the transcripts recovered from long- and short-read sequencing, and the effects of filtering, enabled by sequencing of full-length transcripts, on gene expression. For each sample, we sequenced the same 10x Genomics 3′ complementary DNA (cDNA) using Illumina short reads and Pacific Biosciences long reads and cross-compared each molecule matched through cell barcode and unique molecular identifier. We find that both methods render highly comparable results and recover a large proportion of cells and transcripts. However, platform-dependent cDNA library processing and data analysis steps introduce biases. Short-read sequencing provided higher sequencing depth, but long-read sequencing allowed for retaining transcripts shorter than 500 bp and for removal of degraded cDNA contaminated by template switching oligos. Filtering of artefacts, identifiable only from full-length transcripts, reduces gene count correlation between the two methods.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of single-cell RNA-seq analyses performance based on long-read sequencing platforms
papers.abstract: Introduction The rapid development of next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) allows for detecting and quantifying gene expression in a high-throughput manner, providing a powerful tool for comprehensively understanding cellular function in various biological processes. However, the NGS-based scRNA-seq only quantifies gene expression and cannot reveal the exact transcript structures (isoforms) of each gene due to the limited read length. On the other hand, the long read length of third-generation sequencing (TGS) technologies, including Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) and Pacific Biosciences (PacBio), enable direct reading of intact cDNA molecules. Objectives Both ONT and PacBio have been used in conjunction with scRNA-seq, but their performance in single-cell analyses has not been systematically evaluated. Methods To address this, we generated ONT and PacBio data from the same single-cell cDNA libraries containing different amount of cells. Results Using NGS as a control, we assessed the performance of each platform in cell type identification. Additionally, the reliability in identifying novel isoforms and allele-specific gene/isoform expression by both platforms was verified, providing a systematic evaluation to design the sequencing strategies in single-cell transcriptome studies. Conclusion Beyond gene expression analysis, which the NGS-based scRNA-seq only affords, TGS-based scRNA-seq achieved gene splicing analyses, identifying novel isoforms. Attribute to higher sequencing quality of PacBio, it outperforms ONT in accuracy of novel transcripts identification and allele-specific gene/isoform expression.

papers.title: Bioinformatics frameworks for single-cell long-read sequencing: unlocking isoform-level resolution
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) plays a key role in regulating gene expression, and its dysregulation is implicated in numerous human diseases, including cancer. While bulk RNA sequencing has advanced our understanding of AS, it cannot capture cellular heterogeneity or reliably reconstruct full-length isoforms, both of which underpin disease mechanisms and therapeutic responses. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is an established and a powerful approach to examine AS landscapes at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of cell-specific aberrant splicing events that may contribute to disease. However, conventional scRNA-seq is limited by short read lengths, often preventing an accurate reconstruction of full-length transcript isoforms. This limitation is addressed by long-read RNA-seq (lrRNA-seq), which can sequence full-length RNA molecules, some exceeding 100 000 nucleotides in length. Thereby, lrRNA-seq enables more accurate characterization of isoform diversity, identification of novel splice variants, quantification of percent spliced-in values, and detection of fusion transcripts. The convergence of single-cell resolution and third-generation sequencing technologies has led to the development of single-cell long-read sequencing (SCLR-seq), a powerful approach that addresses the key constraints of bulk short-read RNA-Seq by providing isoform-level resolution and cell-type specificity. This review explores the growing utility of SCLR-seq, highlighting recent developments in bioinformatics tools and pipelines designed for SCLR-seq data analysis. We discuss how this emerging technology is transforming our understanding of isoform regulation and aberrant splicing in human diseases, and its potential to uncover novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Benchmarking long-read RNA-sequencing analysis tools using in silico mixtures
papers.abstract: The lack of benchmark data sets with inbuilt ground-truth makes it challenging to compare the performance of existing long-read isoform detection and differential expression analysis workflows. Here, we present a benchmark experiment using two human lung adenocarcinoma cell lines that were each profiled in triplicate together with synthetic, spliced, spike-in RNAs (sequins). Samples were deeply sequenced on both Illumina short-read and Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read platforms. Alongside the ground-truth available via the sequins, we created in silico mixture samples to allow performance assessment in the absence of true positives or true negatives. Our results show that StringTie2 and bambu outperformed other tools from the six isoform detection tools tested, DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom were best among the five differential transcript expression tools tested and there was no clear front-runner for performing differential transcript usage analysis between the five tools compared, which suggests further methods development is needed for this application.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of Nanopore long-read RNA sequencing for transcript-level analysis in human cell lines
papers.abstract: The human genome contains instructions to transcribe more than 200,000 RNAs. However, many RNA transcripts are generated from the same gene, resulting in alternative isoforms that are highly similar and that remain difficult to quantify. To evaluate the ability to study RNA transcript expression, we profiled seven human cell lines with five different RNA-sequencing protocols, including short-read cDNA, Nanopore long-read direct RNA, amplification-free direct cDNA and PCR-amplified cDNA sequencing, and PacBio IsoSeq, with multiple spike-in controls, and additional transcriptome-wide N6-methyladenosine profiling data. We describe differences in read length, coverage, throughput and transcript expression, reporting that long-read RNA sequencing more robustly identifies major isoforms. We illustrate the value of the SG-NEx data to identify alternative isoforms, novel transcripts, fusion transcripts and N6-methyladenosine RNA modifications. Together, the SG-NEx data provide a comprehensive resource enabling the development and benchmarking of computational methods for profiling complex transcriptional events at isoform-level resolution.

concepts.label: Single-cell long-read transcriptomics
concepts.description: The application of long-read sequencing technologies (e.g., Oxford Nanopore) to single-cell RNA-seq, enabling full-length transcript coverage and accurate isoform detection at single-cell resolution.

concepts.label: Alternative splicing
concepts.description: A regulatory mechanism by which a single gene gives rise to multiple mRNA isoforms, increasing transcriptomic complexity; its resolution at single-cell level is a key motivation for long-read sequencing.

concepts.label: UMI error correction
concepts.description: Computational strategies to correct errors in unique molecular identifier (UMI) sequences caused by sequencing errors, improving accuracy of gene and transcript quantification.

concepts.label: Barcode identification
concepts.description: The process of detecting and assigning cell-specific barcodes from long-read data to separate reads originating from different cells or spatial spots.

concepts.label: Isoform quantification
concepts.description: The estimation of abundances of transcript isoforms using long-read sequencing, enabling differential isoform usage analysis.

concepts.label: Benchmarking workflow
concepts.description: A systematic evaluation framework, implemented as a Nextflow pipeline (scKeñver), to compare computational methods for single-cell and spatial long-read RNA-seq data analysis.

concepts.label: Hybrid methods
concepts.description: Computational methods that leverage paired short-read data to guide barcode and UMI assignment from long-read data.

concepts.label: Long-read-only methods
concepts.description: Computational methods that perform barcode and UMI assignment using only long-read data, without short-read reference.

concepts.label: Isoform-specific methods
concepts.description: Methods that focus on transcript-level analysis, including isoform detection, quantification, and differential usage, often building upon preprocessing from other tools.

concepts.label: Spatial transcriptomics
concepts.description: Gene expression profiling in spatially resolved tissue sections, here using Visium platform with long-read sequencing.

concepts.label: Sequencing depth
concepts.description: The total number of reads generated in a sequencing experiment, affecting sensitivity and method performance.

concepts.label: LongBench dataset
concepts.description: A matched multi-platform reference dataset for benchmarking long-read RNA-seq, covering bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus transcriptomics across eight lung cancer cell lines with synthetic spike-in controls.

concepts.label: Long-read RNA-seq
concepts.description: Sequencing technology producing reads of thousands of base pairs, enabling full-length transcript profiling. Platforms include PacBio (HiFi) and Oxford Nanopore.

concepts.label: Transcript-level quantification
concepts.description: Estimation of expression levels for individual transcript isoforms, which suffers from platform-specific biases and read-to-transcript ambiguity.

concepts.label: Allele-specific analysis
concepts.description: Haplotype-resolved analysis of expression and splicing using phased variants from long reads, allowing detection of cis-regulatory effects and allele-specific isoform usage.

concepts.label: Synthetic spike-in controls
concepts.description: Synthetic RNA molecules (Sequins, SIRVs) added to samples at known concentrations to serve as ground truth for evaluating quantification accuracy and identifying biases.

concepts.label: Read-to-transcript ambiguity
concepts.description: The difficulty in correctly assigning reads to transcript isoforms when multiple isoforms share common exons; long reads reduce this ambiguity compared to short reads.

concepts.label: Internal priming
concepts.description: The phenomenon where reverse transcriptase primes on internal A-rich regions within pre-mRNA rather than the poly-A tail, leading to reads from intronic regions. Commonly observed in PacBio datasets.

concepts.label: cDNA molecule matching
concepts.description: A method to directly compare the same original cDNA molecules sequenced by both short-read and long-read platforms by matching cell barcode and UMI tags, enabling a per-molecule cross-comparison of sequencing readouts.

concepts.label: MAS-ISO-seq
concepts.description: A PacBio long-read sequencing protocol (now Kinnex full-length RNA sequencing) that concatenates full-length cDNA transcripts into longer fragments for high-throughput single-cell isoform sequencing, enabling full-length transcript resolution.

concepts.label: Artefact filtering of long reads
concepts.description: The process of removing artefactual isoforms from long-read data, including intra-priming, RT-switching, and low-coverage non-canonical (LCNC) isoforms, which is enabled by full-length transcript information but may over-filter and bias results against long transcripts.

concepts.label: Cell barcode and UMI counting
concepts.description: The use of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) and cell barcodes to tag and deduplicate transcripts from single cells, allowing accurate gene expression quantification from both short- and long-read sequencing data.

concepts.label: Sequencing platform bias
concepts.description: Differences in library preparation and data analysis inherent to Illumina (short-read) and PacBio (long-read) platforms that affect transcript recovery, gene expression quantification, and cell calling, including GC bias, read length, and filtering stringency.

concepts.label: Third-generation sequencing (TGS)
concepts.description: Long-read sequencing technologies (ONT and PacBio) that sequence intact cDNA molecules, enabling full-length transcript capture and isoform-level analysis in single-cell RNA-seq.

concepts.label: Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq)
concepts.description: A technique to profile gene expression at single-cell resolution, here used with NGS and TGS platforms to compare performance in cell type identification and transcript diversity.

concepts.label: Isoform-level analysis
concepts.description: The ability to identify and quantify transcript isoforms, including novel isoforms, enabled by long-read sequencing, which NGS cannot achieve due to short reads.

concepts.label: Allele-specific expression (ASE)
concepts.description: Detection of transcript expression from each parental allele using SNPs, facilitated by long reads that span multiple variant sites, allowing analysis of allelic bias in gene and isoform expression.

concepts.label: Cell type identification
concepts.description: Unsupervised clustering and marker gene-based assignment of cell types from scRNA-seq data, compared across NGS, ONT, and PacBio platforms to assess accuracy and consistency.

concepts.label: Novel transcript discovery
concepts.description: Identification of previously unannotated transcript isoforms using long-read sequencing, validated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing, with PacBio showing higher accuracy than ONT.

concepts.label: Alternative Splicing
concepts.description: Alternative splicing is a regulatory mechanism that generates multiple transcript isoforms from a single gene, contributing to proteomic diversity and cell-specific gene expression. Its dysregulation is implicated in many diseases, including cancer.

concepts.label: Single-cell RNA-seq
concepts.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing captures transcriptomes of individual cells, enabling analysis of cellular heterogeneity and rare cell types. However, conventional short-read scRNA-seq cannot accurately reconstruct full-length isoforms.

concepts.label: Long-read RNA-seq
concepts.description: Long-read RNA-seq sequences full-length RNA molecules, enabling accurate characterization of isoform diversity, novel splice variants, and fusion transcripts. It is also known as third-generation sequencing.

concepts.label: Single-cell long-read sequencing
concepts.description: SCLR-seq combines single-cell resolution with third-generation sequencing to capture full-length isoforms at single-cell level, overcoming limitations of short-read scRNA-seq and bulk long-read methods.

concepts.label: Cell barcode and UMI
concepts.description: Cell barcodes (CBs) and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are oligonucleotide sequences incorporated during library preparation to label transcripts by cell of origin and to identify PCR duplicates. Accurate recovery of CBs and UMIs is crucial for SCLR-seq analysis.

concepts.label: Isoform quantification
concepts.description: The process of reconstructing full-length transcripts from mapped reads and assigning expression levels to each isoform in individual cells. It involves transcript assembly and quantification, and is a key step in SCLR-seq data analysis.

concepts.label: Differential isoform expression
concepts.description: Analysis of differences in isoform abundance between cell types, conditions, or diseases, revealing cell-type-specific splicing and regulatory mechanisms. It includes differential transcript usage (DTU) and percent spliced-in (PSI) metrics.

concepts.label: In silico mixtures
concepts.description: Computational mixtures of sequencing reads from two pure cell line samples at defined proportions (e.g., 75:25, 50:50, 25:75) that create samples with known biological differences, allowing performance evaluation of differential analysis tools without requiring additional experimental mixtures.

concepts.label: Sequins
concepts.description: Synthetic spliced spike-in RNAs with known sequences, abundance, and splicing patterns that are added to RNA samples to provide ground-truth for evaluating the accuracy of isoform detection, quantification, and differential analysis methods.

concepts.label: Differential transcript expression (DTE)
concepts.description: Analysis that tests for changes in the absolute expression level of individual transcripts between experimental conditions, using transcript-level count data from RNA-seq.

concepts.label: Differential transcript usage (DTU)
concepts.description: Analysis that examines whether the relative abundance of transcripts from the same gene differs between conditions, reflecting changes in splicing or transcript proportion.

concepts.label: Transcript assignment ambiguity
concepts.description: Uncertainty in assigning sequencing reads (especially short reads) to specific transcript isoforms due to shared exons, quantified by over-dispersion; lower in long-read data due to longer reads spanning multiple splice junctions.

concepts.label: Major isoform
concepts.description: The most abundantly expressed transcript for a given gene in a specific cell line or condition. The paper demonstrates that long-read RNA-seq identifies major isoforms more robustly than short-read RNA-seq, with experimental validation confirming their higher abundance.

concepts.label: Full-splice-match read
concepts.description: A long read that spans all exon junctions of a transcript, providing unambiguous evidence for the complete isoform structure. The paper uses full-splice-match reads to identify alternative isoforms, fusion transcripts, and complex splicing events.

concepts.label: Isoform switching
concepts.description: A change in the dominant isoform expressed from a gene across different cell lines or conditions. The paper identifies cell-type-specific isoform switching events involving multiple exon-level changes, such as alternative promoters and splicing.

concepts.label: Spike-in controls
concepts.description: Synthetic RNA molecules of known concentration added to samples to evaluate quantification accuracy. The paper uses ERCC, SIRVs, Sequin, and long SIRV spike-ins to benchmark gene and transcript expression estimates across protocols.

concepts.label: RNA fragmentation bias
concepts.description: The systematic distortion in transcript abundance estimates caused by breaking RNA molecules into shorter fragments during library preparation. The paper shows that fragmentation inflates expression estimates for certain isoforms in short-read RNA-seq, leading to discordant major isoform calls.

tools.name: wf-single-cell
tools.description: Oxford Nanopore's workflow for single-cell RNA-seq analysis, performing barcode detection, UMI correction and clustering, gene expression quantification, and isoform analysis.

tools.name: FLAMES
tools.description: Single-cell long-read analysis tool that handles read alignment, UMI deduplication, isoform quantification and discovery.

tools.name: Sicelore 2.1
tools.description: Long-read-only tool for barcode identification and UMI correction, using a consensus sequence approach and strict transcript assignment.

tools.name: scNanoGPS
tools.description: Long-read-only tool that uses the iCARLO algorithm for barcode correction and UMI clustering.

tools.name: Bambu
tools.description: R package for isoform quantification and discovery from long-read RNA-seq, using splice alignment correction and without UMI error correction.

tools.name: Isosceles
tools.description: Method for transcript-level analysis from single-cell long-read data, including isoform quantification and differential usage, building on preprocessing from tools like Sicelore or wf-single-cell.

tools.name: IsoQuant
tools.description: Method for reference-guided de novo isoform detection and quantification from single-cell long-read data, often used with wf-single-cell preprocessing.

tools.name: Sicelore (hybrid)
tools.description: Hybrid method that uses paired short-read data to guide barcode and UMI assignment from long-reads.

tools.name: Snuupy
tools.description: Hybrid method that improves on Sicelore by removing dependency on poly-A tail detection.

tools.name: scNapBar
tools.description: Hybrid method that aims to reduce dependency on short-read sequencing depth.

tools.name: BLAZE
tools.description: Tool for barcode detection in long-read single-cell data, used by FLAMES and other methods.

tools.name: flexiplex
tools.description: Tool for barcode and UMI detection from long reads, used by Bambu.

tools.name: AsaruSim
tools.description: Simulation tool for generating realistic single-cell long-read RNA-seq data with known ground truth.

tools.name: scKeñver
tools.description: Nextflow-based reproducible benchmarking workflow developed in this study for evaluating single-cell long-read methods.

tools.name: Isoswitch
tools.description: R package for detecting differential isoform usage (isoform switches) between cell clusters.

tools.name: UMI-tools
tools.description: Toolkit for UMI deduplication, including directional graph method used by wf-single-cell.

tools.name: PrimeSpotter
tools.description: A custom tool to identify reads likely resulting from internal priming at genomically encoded A stretches within transcripts.

tools.name: Clair3-RNA
tools.description: A variant caller for long-read RNA-seq data.

tools.name: WhatsHap
tools.description: A tool for phasing variants from sequencing data.

tools.name: LongcallR
tools.description: A tool for haplotype-resolved allele-specific expression and splicing analysis using long reads.

tools.name: ONT PCR-cDNA
tools.description: Oxford Nanopore Technologies protocol using PCR-amplified cDNA libraries for long-read sequencing.

tools.name: ONT direct RNA
tools.description: Oxford Nanopore Technologies protocol for direct sequencing of native RNA molecules, enabling detection of RNA modifications.

tools.name: PacBio Kinnex
tools.description: Pacific Biosciences high-throughput cDNA sequencing protocol using concatenated circular inserts.

tools.name: Illumina short-read sequencing
tools.description: Standard short-read sequencing used as a reference in the benchmark.

tools.name: 10X Genomics Chromium
tools.description: Platform for single-cell and single-nucleus library preparation used with long-read and short-read sequencing.

tools.name: MAS-ISO-seq (Kinnex full-length RNA sequencing)
tools.description: A PacBio library preparation method that concatenates multiple full-length cDNA transcripts into long fragments for sequencing on PacBio instruments, enabling single-cell isoform-resolution transcriptomics.

tools.name: CellRanger
tools.description: A popular software pipeline by 10x Genomics for processing single-cell short-read sequencing data, performing cell calling, UMI counting, and gene expression quantification.

tools.name: SMRTLink Iso-Seq single-cell pipeline
tools.description: A PacBio software pipeline for processing single-cell long-read sequencing data, including read segmentation, cell barcode correction, deduplication, and isoform classification via SQANTI and pigeon.

tools.name: BLAZE
tools.description: A tool for empty droplet detection in single-cell sequencing data, used in this study to classify low-quality cell barcodes in PacBio data.

tools.name: SQANTI3
tools.description: A tool for quality control and classification of long-read transcriptome data, categorizing isoforms into structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, etc.) and identifying artefacts.

tools.name: pigeon
tools.description: The annotation tool within the SMRTLink Iso-Seq pipeline used for generating gene-level and isoform-level count matrices from PacBio data, applying isoform classification and artefact filtering.

tools.name: Longbow
tools.description: Official software used to extract full-length transcript fragments (FLTs) from PacBio sequencing reads in the study.

tools.name: IsoQuant
tools.description: Tool used to classify isoform types (consistent match, inconsistency, misalignment) by aligning reads to reference sequences for evaluating isoform identification accuracy.

tools.name: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION
tools.description: Long-read sequencing platform used to generate single-cell cDNA reads; evaluated for cell barcode detection, gene expression, and isoform identification.

tools.name: PacBio Sequel IIe (MAS-ISO-seq)
tools.description: Long-read sequencing platform with circular consensus sequencing (CCS) and MAS-ISO-seq for multiplexing; evaluated for accuracy in cell type identification, novel isoform discovery, and allele-specific expression.

tools.name: MGISEQ-2000
tools.description: Short-read NGS platform used as a benchmark for comparison with TGS platforms in single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

tools.name: FLAMES
tools.description: Full-length analysis of single-cell long-read sequencing data; an end-to-end pipeline that integrates barcode extraction, transcript assembly, and quantification. It is designed for ONT data and supports multiple single-cell protocols.

tools.name: SiCeLoRe
tools.description: A pipeline for processing SCLR-seq data that handles chimeric reads, identifies cell barcodes and UMIs, and performs isoform quantification. It uses accompanying short-read data for error correction.

tools.name: BLAZE
tools.description: A tool for barcode extraction and demultiplexing from SCLR-seq data without requiring a known barcode whitelist. It identifies poly-T signals and adapters to extract CBs and UMIs.

tools.name: Flexiplex
tools.description: An error-tolerant barcode and UMI search tool that also splits chimeric reads. It works with UMI-based single-cell protocols and does not require known barcodes.

tools.name: Longcell
tools.description: UMI deduplication and isoform quantification tool that uses iterative clustering to correct UMI sequences and recover accurate barcodes. It also helps correct mapping and truncation errors.

tools.name: SCOTCH
tools.description: A modular toolkit for isoform reconstruction from long reads, compatible with ONT and PacBio platforms. It uses sub-exon identification with dynamic thresholding to resolve ambiguous mappings.

tools.name: Isosceles
tools.description: An R package for splice graph-based isoform detection and quantification from ONT SCLR-seq data. It supports downstream analyses like differential transcript usage.

tools.name: lr-kallisto
tools.description: A pseudoalignment approach for long-read RNA-seq data that is robust to sequencing errors. It can be used for transcript discovery and quantification.

tools.name: Oarfish
tools.description: A probabilistic isoform quantification tool for UMI-based single-cell long-read data. It is fast and computationally efficient.

tools.name: SQANTI3
tools.description: A tool for classifying and filtering isoforms from long-read sequencing data by comparing splice junctions to annotations. It categorizes isoforms into known and novel categories and filters technical artifacts.

tools.name: Minimap2
tools.description: A widely used aligner for long-read sequencing that supports spliced alignment and retains barcode and UMI tags in the BAM output.

tools.name: ScisorWiz
tools.description: A visualization tool for differential isoform expression across cell clusters from single-cell long-read sequencing data.

tools.name: bambu
tools.description: Isoform detection and quantification tool for long-read RNA-seq that uses supervised and unsupervised analysis; in the full data set, it achieved the highest recall (~0.91) and precision (~0.62) for sequin transcript detection.

tools.name: Cupcake
tools.description: Isoform detection pipeline that collapses and deduplicates cDNA sequences; in this study it detected many artifactual isoforms and had low precision.

tools.name: FLAIR
tools.description: Isoform detection tool that uses long-read alignments to identify isoforms; it had low precision in the benchmark but high recall for retained isoforms.

tools.name: FLAMES
tools.description: Isoform detection and quantification tool for long reads; in the downsampled analysis it had the second highest precision after StringTie2.

tools.name: StringTie2
tools.description: Isoform detection and quantification tool that can use both long and short reads; in the downsampled analysis it recovered 80% of removed sequins with the highest precision.

tools.name: TALON
tools.description: Isoform detection tool that uses long-read data to refine transcript annotations; it had low precision but high recall for known isoforms.

tools.name: DESeq2
tools.description: Differential expression analysis method using negative binomial modeling; it performed well for DTE on long-read data with good sensitivity and FDR control.

tools.name: edgeR (DTE pipeline)
tools.description: Differential expression analysis using edgeR's quasi-likelihood pipeline; it performed well for DTE on long-read data, balancing power and FDR control.

tools.name: EBSeq
tools.description: Differential expression method using Bayesian approach; it detected the fewest DTEs but had good FDR control on sequins data.

tools.name: limma-voom
tools.description: Differential expression pipeline using linear modeling with voom precision weights; it performed similarly to DESeq2 and edgeR for DTE on long-read data.

tools.name: NOISeq
tools.description: Differential expression method based on noise distribution; it detected many DTEs but had high FDR on sequins.

tools.name: DRIMSeq
tools.description: Differential transcript usage method using Dirichlet-multinomial model; it detected many DTU transcripts but had high FDR.

tools.name: satuRn
tools.description: Differential transcript usage method using quasi-binomial generalized additive model; it had moderate power and FDR control.

tools.name: DEXSeq
tools.description: Differential exon usage method that can be used for DTU on transcript-level counts; it had high sensitivity but also high FDR.

tools.name: limma-diffSplice
tools.description: Differential splicing pipeline using limma; it detected fewer DTU features than others but had lower FDR.

tools.name: edgeR-diffSpliceDGE
tools.description: Differential splicing pipeline using edgeR; it had the best FDR control for DTU on sequins but the lowest power.

tools.name: Salmon
tools.description: Transcript quantification tool for RNA-seq; used to quantify sequins and human transcripts for comparison, showing high correlation with expected abundances for sequins.

tools.name: GENCODE
tools.description: Reference human gene annotation (Release 33) used as the transcript reference for mapping and quantification in the benchmark.

tools.name: nf-core/nanoseq
tools.description: A community-curated Nextflow pipeline for streamlined processing of Nanopore long-read RNA-seq data. It integrates quality control, alignment, transcript discovery, quantification, differential expression, fusion detection, and RNA modification detection modules.

tools.name: Bambu
tools.description: A computational method for transcript discovery and quantification from long-read RNA-seq data. It is used in the SG-NEx pipeline for isoform quantification and fusion transcript analysis.

tools.name: JAFFAL
tools.description: A tool for fusion gene detection from long-read RNA-seq data. It identifies fusion genes and assigns genomic breakpoints, used in the SG-NEx study to discover fusion transcripts.

tools.name: m6Anet
tools.description: A deep learning method for detecting N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modifications from Nanopore direct RNA-seq data. It was used to predict m6A positions across the SG-NEx cell lines.

tools.name: SQANTI3
tools.description: A tool for filtering and classifying novel transcripts from long-read RNA-seq data. It was used to remove potential artifacts such as reverse transcription switching and intra-priming in the SG-NEx novel transcript analysis.

tools.name: Salmon
tools.description: A computational tool for quantifying transcript expression from RNA-seq data. It was used in the SG-NEx study to estimate gene and transcript expression from both short-read and long-read data for benchmarking.

## Papers

## Paper: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq Nanopore long-read data

### Key Concepts
- Single-cell long-read transcriptomics: Application of long-read sequencing to single-cell RNA-seq for full-length transcript coverage.
- Alternative splicing: Key biological process driving transcriptomic complexity, resolved by long reads.
- UMI error correction: Strategies to correct sequencing errors in Unique Molecular Identifiers.
- Barcode identification: Process of assigning cell-specific barcodes from long-read data.
- Isoform quantification: Estimation of transcript abundances at isoform level.
- Benchmarking workflow: Nextflow-based framework (scKeñver) for systematic method comparison.
- Hybrid methods: Methods using short-read data to guide long-read preprocessing.
- Long-read-only methods: Methods processing long reads independently.
- Isoform-specific methods: Focused on transcript-level analysis.
- Spatial transcriptomics: Gene expression profiling in spatial context using Visium + long reads.

### Tools / Methods
- wf-single-cell: ONT pipeline for barcode/UMI detection, gene and isoform quantification.
- FLAMES: Single-cell long-read analysis tool.
- Sicelore 2.1: UMI correction and transcript assignment with consensus.
- scNanoGPS: Uses iCARLO algorithm for barcode correction.
- Bambu: Isoform quantification and discovery without UMI correction.
- Isosceles: Isoform analysis building on preprocessing from other tools.
- IsoQuant: Reference-guided isoform detection.
- Sicelore (hybrid): Uses short-read data for barcode/UMI assignment.
- Snuupy: Hybrid method improving on Sicelore.
- scNapBar: Hybrid method reducing short-read dependency.
- BLAZE: Barcode detection for long reads.
- flexiplex: Barcode/UMI detection for long reads.
- AsaruSim: Simulation tool for sc long-read data.
- scKeñver: Benchmarking workflow.
- Isoswitch: Differential isoform usage detection.
- UMI-tools: Toolkit used by wf-single-cell.

### Main Findings
- Long-read-only methods perform well across datasets, making paired short-read data unnecessary.
- Tool performance depends on sequencing depth and quality (e.g., R10.4.1 chemistry improves results).
- wf-single-cell excels in gene expression quantification and UMI correction; Bambu and Isosceles lead in isoform discovery.
- Long-read methods can outperform short-read CellRanger for cell type annotation due to 3' bias in short reads.
- Short-read data is not a perfect gold standard; long-read methods show higher sensitivity in gene detection.
- The benchmark provides a reusable workflow (scKeñver) for future method evaluation.

## Paper: Benchmarking long-read RNA-sequencing technologies with LongBench: a cross-platform reference dataset profiling cancer cell lines with bulk and single-cell approaches

### Key Concepts
- LongBench dataset: A matched multi-platform reference dataset for benchmarking long-read RNA-seq across bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus transcriptomics.
- Long-read RNA-seq: Sequencing technology producing long reads enabling full-length transcript profiling.
- Transcript-level quantification: Estimation of expression for individual isoforms, hindered by platform-specific biases.
- Allele-specific analysis: Haplotype-resolved detection of expression and splicing differences using long-read phased variants.
- Synthetic spike-in controls: Ground truth molecules for assessing quantification accuracy.
- Read-to-transcript ambiguity: The reduced ambiguity in isoform assignment with long reads compared to short reads.
- Internal priming: Reverse transcription priming on internal A-rich regions, leading to intronic reads especially in PacBio.

### Tools / Methods
- ONT PCR-cDNA: Oxford Nanopore protocol using PCR-amplified cDNA.
- ONT direct RNA: Oxford Nanopore protocol for native RNA sequencing.
- PacBio Kinnex: Pacific Biosciences high-throughput cDNA sequencing.
- Illumina short-read: Reference sequencing using short reads.
- 10X Genomics Chromium: Single-cell/nucleus library preparation.
- PrimeSpotter: Tool for detecting internal priming.
- Clair3-RNA: Variant caller for long-read RNA-seq.
- WhatsHap: Variant phasing tool.
- LongcallR: Tool for allele-specific expression and splicing analysis.

### Main Findings
- High concordance in gene-level differential expression across platforms, but reduced consistency at transcript level.
- PacBio Kinnex has higher accuracy and throughput but shows internal priming and underrepresentation of short transcripts.
- ONT cDNA is less costly but yields shorter, less accurate reads and misses longer transcripts.
- ONT direct RNA has lowest bias and enables detection of RNA modifications, but requires high input.
- Single-cell long-read data are highly concordant with bulk; single-nucleus data show reduced feature detection.
- Long reads enable robust variant phasing and allele-specific analyses.
- LongBench is one of the largest publicly available long-read benchmarking datasets.

## Paper: Comparison of single-cell long-read and short-read transcriptome sequencing via cDNA molecule matching: quality evaluation of the MAS-ISO-seq approach
### Key Concepts
- cDNA molecule matching: Direct comparison of same cDNA molecules sequenced by both platforms using barcode/UMI tags.
- MAS-ISO-seq: PacBio protocol for single-cell long-read isoform sequencing.
- Artefact filtering: Removal of intra-priming, RT-switching, and LCNC isoforms enabled by full-length reads.
- Cell barcode and UMI counting: Tagging molecules for deduplication and quantification.
- Sequencing platform bias: Differences in library prep and analysis affecting transcript recovery.
### Tools / Methods
- MAS-ISO-seq (Kinnex): Long-read library preparation method.
- CellRanger: Illumina short-read processing pipeline.
- SMRTLink Iso-Seq pipeline: PacBio long-read processing pipeline.
- BLAZE: Empty droplet detection tool.
- SQANTI3: Isoform classification and quality control.
- pigeon: Annotation tool for generating count matrices.
### Main Findings
- Both methods yield highly comparable results, with 90% gene overlap and strong correlation.
- Short-read data has higher depth but includes more low-quality cells and multi-mapping reads.
- Long-read data retains short transcripts (<500 bp) and allows artefact removal, but filtering biases against long genes.
- Artefact filtering reduces gene count correlation between the two methods.
- The choice between methods depends on research focus: isoform resolution vs. cost and depth.

## Paper: Systematic evaluation of single-cell RNA-seq analyses performance based on long-read sequencing platforms
### Key Concepts
- Third-generation sequencing (TGS): Long-read sequencing technologies (ONT and PacBio) that sequence intact cDNA molecules, enabling full-length transcript capture and isoform-level analysis in single-cell RNA-seq.
- Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq): A technique to profile gene expression at single-cell resolution, here used with NGS and TGS platforms to compare performance in cell type identification and transcript diversity.
- Isoform-level analysis: The ability to identify and quantify transcript isoforms, including novel isoforms, enabled by long-read sequencing, which NGS cannot achieve due to short reads.
- Allele-specific expression (ASE): Detection of transcript expression from each parental allele using SNPs, facilitated by long reads that span multiple variant sites, allowing analysis of allelic bias in gene and isoform expression.
- Cell type identification: Unsupervised clustering and marker gene-based assignment of cell types from scRNA-seq data, compared across NGS, ONT, and PacBio platforms to assess accuracy and consistency.
- Novel transcript discovery: Identification of previously unannotated transcript isoforms using long-read sequencing, validated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing, with PacBio showing higher accuracy than ONT.
### Tools / Methods
- Longbow: Official software used to extract full-length transcript fragments (FLTs) from PacBio sequencing reads.
- IsoQuant: Tool used to classify isoform types (consistent match, inconsistency, misalignment) by aligning reads to reference sequences for evaluating isoform identification accuracy.
- Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION: Long-read sequencing platform used to generate single-cell cDNA reads; evaluated for cell barcode detection, gene expression, and isoform identification.
- PacBio Sequel IIe (MAS-ISO-seq): Long-read sequencing platform with circular consensus sequencing (CCS) and MAS-ISO-seq for multiplexing; evaluated for accuracy in cell type identification, novel isoform discovery, and allele-specific expression.
- MGISEQ-2000: Short-read NGS platform used as a benchmark for comparison with TGS platforms in single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
### Main Findings
- TGS-based scRNA-seq can independently generate single-cell gene/isoform expression matrices and accurately capture all cell types despite lower gene detection sensitivity due to limited throughput.
- PacBio demonstrates superior performance over ONT in discovering novel transcripts and in allele-specific gene/isoform expression analysis, attributed to higher sequencing quality.
- Both TGS platforms enable isoform-level and allele-specific analyses that are not possible with NGS-based scRNA-seq, providing additional insights into transcript diversity and regulation.
- For a given sequencing yield, using more cells in a library (up to ~5000) yields more cell-type-specific DEGs and DEIs than fewer cells with higher per-cell coverage.

## Paper: Bioinformatics frameworks for single-cell long-read sequencing: unlocking isoform-level resolution

### Key Concepts
- Alternative Splicing: Key regulatory mechanism driving transcript diversity; dysregulation linked to disease.
- Single-cell RNA-seq: Captures cellular heterogeneity but limited by short reads.
- Long-read RNA-seq: Sequences full-length transcripts, enabling accurate isoform characterization.
- Single-cell long-read sequencing (SCLR-seq): Combines single-cell and long-read technologies for isoform-level resolution.
- Cell barcode and UMI: Essential for demultiplexing and deduplication in single-cell experiments.
- Isoform quantification: Reconstructing and quantifying full-length isoforms from SCLR-seq data.
- Differential isoform expression: Analyzing changes in isoform usage across cell types and conditions.

### Tools/Methods
- FLAMES: End-to-end pipeline for ONT-based SCLR-seq data analysis.
- SiCeLoRe: Pipeline with chimera handling and barcode/UMI identification.
- BLAZE: Fast barcode extraction and demultiplexing without known whitelist.
- Flexiplex: Error-tolerant barcode search and chimera splitting.
- Longcell: UMI deduplication and isoform quantification with iterative clustering.
- SCOTCH: Modular toolkit for isoform reconstruction platform-agnostic.
- Isosceles: R package for splice graph-based isoform discovery and quantification.
- lr-kallisto: Pseudoalignment for long reads, robust to errors.
- Oarfish: Probabilistic isoform quantification.
- SQANTI3: Isoform classification and filtering using structural features.
- Minimap2: Long-read aligner retaining barcode tags.

### Main Findings
- SCLR-seq overcomes limitations of short-read scRNA-seq by providing full-length isoform information at single-cell resolution.
- The proliferation of bioinformatics tools has addressed key challenges in barcode recovery, transcript assembly, and isoform quantification.
- SCLR-seq has been applied to study alternative splicing in cancer, neurodevelopment, and other diseases, revealing novel isoforms and splicing events.
- Challenges remain, including high error rates, data sparsity, and computational costs, but ongoing developments are improving accessibility and accuracy.
- Integration with other modalities (e.g., ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics) promises deeper insights into gene regulation.

## Paper: Benchmarking long-read RNA-sequencing analysis tools using in silico mixtures

### Key Concepts
- **In silico mixtures**: Computational mixtures of reads from pure cell lines at known proportions, enabling ground-truth evaluation without extra experiments.
- **Sequins**: Synthetic spliced spike-in RNAs with known abundance and splicing, providing ground-truth for isoform detection and quantification.
- **Differential transcript expression (DTE)**: Tests for absolute expression changes of transcripts between conditions.
- **Differential transcript usage (DTU)**: Tests for relative proportion changes of transcripts from the same gene.
- **Transcript assignment ambiguity**: Uncertainty in assigning reads to isoforms, quantified by over-dispersion; lower in long-read data.

### Tools / Methods
- **bambu**: Isoform detection and quantification; highest recall and precision on sequins in full data.
- **Cupcake**: Isoform detection pipeline; detected many artifactual isoforms.
- **FLAIR**: Isoform detection; low precision but high recall for retained isoforms.
- **FLAMES**: Isoform detection and quantification; second highest precision in downsampled analysis.
- **StringTie2**: Isoform detection and quantification; recovered 80% of removed sequins with highest precision in downsampled analysis.
- **TALON**: Isoform detection; low precision but high recall for known isoforms.
- **DESeq2, edgeR (DTE), limma-voom**: Best performing DTE methods with balanced sensitivity and FDR.
- **EBSeq, NOISeq**: Other DTE methods; EBSeq had low power, NOISeq had high FDR.
- **DRIMSeq, satuRn, DEXSeq, limma-diffSplice, edgeR-diffSpliceDGE**: DTU methods; no clear front-runner, with edgeR-diffSpliceDGE best FDR control but lowest power.
- **Salmon**: Quantification tool used for transcript abundance estimation.
- **GENCODE**: Reference human annotation (Release 33).

### Main Findings
- **Isoform detection**: StringTie2 and bambu outperform other tools; StringTie2 had best accuracy, bambu best power.
- **DTE analysis**: DESeq2, edgeR, and limma-voom perform well on long-read data, similar to short-read gold standards.
- **DTU analysis**: No method simultaneously achieves high power and low FDR; further method development needed.
- **In silico mixtures** effectively replicate physical mixtures, saving 60% sequencing cost.
- **Long-read data** shows lower transcript assignment ambiguity (over-dispersion ~1.15) compared to Illumina (over-dispersion >3.56).
- **10 million reads per sample** sufficient to recover >50% of DTE discoveries from full data.
- **Orthogonal validation** using short reads reveals many novel junctions from long-read tools lack support, indicating overprediction.

## Paper: A systematic benchmark of Nanopore long-read RNA sequencing for transcript-level analysis in human cell lines
### Key Concepts
- Major isoform: The most abundant transcript for a gene; long-read RNA-seq identifies it more robustly than short-read.
- Full-splice-match read: A read spanning all exon junctions, providing unambiguous isoform evidence.
- Isoform switching: Change in dominant isoform across cell lines, often involving multiple exon-level events.
- Spike-in controls: Synthetic RNAs of known concentration used to benchmark quantification accuracy.
- RNA fragmentation bias: Distortion in transcript estimates due to RNA fragmentation, inflating short-read major isoforms.
### Tools / Methods
- nf-core/nanoseq: Community-curated Nextflow pipeline for Nanopore RNA-seq analysis.
- Bambu: Software for transcript discovery and quantification from long-read data.
- JAFFAL: Tool for fusion gene detection from long-read RNA-seq.
- m6Anet: Deep learning method for m6A detection from direct RNA-seq.
- SQANTI3: Tool for filtering novel transcripts from long-read data.
- Salmon: Quantification tool used for both short-read and long-read data.
### Main Findings
- Long-read RNA-seq identifies major isoforms more robustly than short-read, validated by qPCR and dPCR.
- Read fragmentation partially explains discordant transcript estimates between short-read and long-read data.
- The SG-NEx resource enables discovery of alternative isoforms, novel transcripts, fusion transcripts, and m6A modifications.
- Novel transcripts are enriched in repetitive elements.
- Long-read RNA-seq can reconstruct full-length fusion transcripts and detect cell-type-specific m6A sites.

benchmark.question: In the systematic benchmark by Hamraoui et al., which method achieved the highest F1-score in UMI clustering on simulated R9.4.1 data?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: wf-single-cell, with a mean F1-score of 0.8 and highest ARI of 0.81.

benchmark.question: Which hybrid method failed to process the PromethION datasets due to excessive memory usage?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Snuupy, which required up to 200 GB of RAM for the BLAST step and was deemed unsuitable for large-scale datasets.

benchmark.question: According to the benchmark, what is the key advantage of long-read methods over short-read CellRanger for cell type annotation?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Long-read methods like Bambu and wf-single-cell outperform CellRanger because short-read data suffers from 3' bias due to incomplete 3'-UTR annotations, while long-read sequencing enables accurate gene expression quantification across the full transcript, leading to more precise cell-type separation.

benchmark.question: How does the UMI error correction strategy differ between wf-single-cell and Bambu, and what impact does this have on gene expression quantification accuracy?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: wf-single-cell uses a directional graph approach from UMI-tools for UMI clustering, resulting in high-fidelity UMI correction and accurate gene expression estimation. Bambu directly merges raw UMI sequences without error correction, leading to overestimation of expression counts, especially under high sequencing saturation and error rates.

benchmark.question: Which two ONT chemistries were compared in the simulated datasets to assess the impact of sequencing quality on method performance?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: R9.4.1 (median Phred score 13) and R10.4.1 (median Phred score 20), with R10.4.1 showing overall improved method performance.

benchmark.question: Which long-read sequencing protocols are included in the LongBench dataset?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: LongBench includes three long-read protocols: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PCR-cDNA, ONT direct RNA, and PacBio Kinnex.

benchmark.question: What is the name and purpose of the custom tool used in this study to identify reads resulting from internal priming?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: PrimeSpotter is a custom tool that identifies reads likely resulting from internal priming at genomically encoded A stretches within transcripts, rather than at genuine polyA tails.

benchmark.question: According to LongBench, which sequencing platform showed the highest correlation between observed and expected abundances for spike-in controls?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: ONT direct RNA (dRNA) consistently achieved the highest correlation between observed and expected transcript abundances for spike-in controls across all platforms.

benchmark.question: What is the key advantage of long-read RNA-seq over short-read in resolving transcript-level expression?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Long reads reduce read-to-transcript ambiguity, enabling more accurate and stable isoform assignment compared to short reads, especially for multi-isoform genes.

benchmark.question: What is the name of the PacBio long-read sequencing protocol evaluated in this study, and what is its newer name?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: The protocol is called MAS-ISO-seq, which has been relabeled as Kinnex full-length RNA sequencing.

benchmark.question: How did the authors match the same original cDNA molecules between short-read and long-read sequencing data?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: They matched molecules through cell barcode and unique molecular identifier (UMI) tags, enabling a per-molecule cross-comparison of sequencing readouts.

benchmark.question: What tool was used for empty droplet detection in PacBio data, and what percentage of CellRanger-specific cells were classified as empty droplets by this tool?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: BLAZE was used for empty droplet detection in PacBio data. It classified 9%–32% of CellRanger-specific cells as empty droplets.

benchmark.question: What are the three types of artefactual transcripts distinguished by the PacBio pipeline, and which category accounted for the largest proportion of filtered reads?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: The three types are intra-priming, RT-switching, and low coverage/non-canonical (LCNC) isoforms. LCNC accounted for the largest proportion, with an average of 27% of reads and 48% of isoforms filtered.

benchmark.question: What was the effect of artefact filtering on gene count correlation between PacBio and Illumina data, and which genes were most affected?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Artefact filtering reduced the gene count correlation between the two methods (from R > 0.92 to R between 0.9 and 0.95) and biased against longer genes, especially those longer than 4000 bp, leading to a decrease in counts for those genes.

benchmark.question: According to Deng et al., which long-read sequencing platform demonstrated higher accuracy in identifying novel transcripts and allele-specific expression?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: PacBio (Pacific Biosciences) outperformed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) in the accuracy of novel transcript identification and allele-specific gene/isoform expression, attributed to its higher sequencing quality.

benchmark.question: What method was used to validate novel isoforms captured by each TGS platform in this study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Novel isoforms were validated using RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing; 11 out of 15 PacBio-specific transcripts were confirmed compared to 3 out of 14 ONT-specific transcripts.

benchmark.question: What is the name of the software used to extract full-length transcript fragments (FLTs) from PacBio reads in this study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Longbow, the official software, was used to extract FLTs from PacBio sequencing reads.

benchmark.question: How did the study define 'unknown reads' in the context of allele-specific expression analysis?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Unknown reads were defined as reads that did not cover any SNP sites and therefore could not be assigned to a specific parental allele.

benchmark.question: What recommendation does the study make regarding the number of cells per library for TGS-based scRNA-seq when sequencing yield is fixed?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: The study recommends using more cells in a library (up to approximately 5000 cells) rather than maximizing per-cell gene detection, because a larger cell sample yields more cell-type-specific DEGs and DEIs despite lower per-cell gene coverage.

benchmark.question: What is the primary advantage of single-cell long-read sequencing (SCLR-seq) over conventional short-read scRNA-seq?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: SCLR-seq sequences full-length RNA molecules, enabling accurate characterization of isoform diversity, identification of novel splice variants, and quantification of percent spliced-in values at single-cell resolution, overcoming the short-read limitations of conventional scRNA-seq.

benchmark.question: Which two long-read sequencing platforms are primarily used for SCLR-seq, and what is a key trade-off between them?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) are the two main platforms. PacBio provides higher accuracy (up to 99.95% with HiFi reads) but has lower throughput and higher cost, while ONT offers higher throughput and lower cost but has higher error rates.

benchmark.question: Name two end-to-end pipelines for SCLR-seq data analysis and the sequencing platform they are predominantly designed for.
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: FLAMES and SiCeLoRe are two end-to-end pipelines, both predominantly designed for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) data.

benchmark.question: What is the role of SQANTI3 in SCLR-seq analysis, and how does it classify isoforms?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: SQANTI3 classifies and filters isoforms from long-read sequencing data by comparing splice junctions to annotations. It categorizes isoforms into full splice match, incomplete splice match, novel in catalog (NIC), novel not in catalog (NNIC), fusion, intergenic, genic intron, genic genomic, and antisense, and filters technical artifacts.

benchmark.question: What is a key challenge in UMI error correction for SCLR-seq data, and how does Longcell address it?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: A key challenge is UMI crowding, where the edit distance between true UMIs decreases as gene expression increases, leading to ambiguous UMI assignment. Longcell addresses this by using an iterative clustering procedure to cluster putative UMI sequences and correct truncation and mapping errors.

benchmark.question: What sequencing platforms were used in this benchmark study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Illumina short-read and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read platforms.

benchmark.question: In the isoform detection comparison, which two tools performed best and in which aspects?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: bambu achieved the highest recall (~0.91) and precision (~0.62) in the full data set. StringTie2 excelled in the downsampled analysis, recovering 80% of removed sequins with the highest precision.

benchmark.question: How did the authors use in silico mixtures and sequins to evaluate DTE and DTU methods?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: In silico mixtures provided a series of comparisons with known biological differences between pure cell lines, allowing assessment of recovery and inconsistency rates. Sequins provided ground-truth for calculating true positive rate (TPR) and false discovery rate (FDR). Together, they enabled genome-wide and targeted evaluation of differential analysis tools.

benchmark.question: What are sequins and what purpose do they serve in this study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Sequins are synthetic spliced spike-in RNAs with known sequences, abundance, and splicing patterns. They are added to RNA samples to provide ground-truth for evaluating accuracy of isoform detection, quantification, and differential analysis methods.

benchmark.question: What was the main conclusion regarding differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis tools?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: No DTU method achieved a balance between power and false discovery control; DRIMSeq and DEXSeq had high sensitivity but high FDR, while edgeR-diffSpliceDGE had best FDR control but lowest power. The study suggests further method development is needed.

benchmark.question: In the SG-NEx study, which long-read RNA sequencing protocol generated the highest throughput per sample?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: PCR-amplified cDNA sequencing (cDNA protocol) consistently generated the highest throughput per sample among the long-read protocols.

benchmark.question: What is a 'full-splice-match read' and why is it important in the SG-NEx study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: A full-splice-match read is a long read that spans all exon junctions of a transcript, providing unambiguous evidence for the complete isoform structure. It is important because it enables identification of alternative isoforms, fusion transcripts, and complex splicing events.

benchmark.question: How did the authors of the SG-NEx study simulate short-read RNA-seq from long-read data to assess the impact of fragmentation on transcript quantification?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: They aligned long reads to the transcriptome, performed error correction using the reference transcriptome sequence, and then sampled 150-bp error-corrected, short (fragmented) reads from these long reads to create matched long-read, fragmented long-read (simulated short-read), and Illumina short-read data for 67 SG-NEx samples.

benchmark.question: Which tool was used in the SG-NEx study for fusion gene detection from long-read RNA-seq data?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: JAFFAL was used for fusion gene detection from long-read RNA-seq data.

benchmark.question: What was the key finding regarding major isoform identification when comparing long-read and short-read RNA-seq in the SG-NEx study?
benchmark.ground_truth_answer: Long-read RNA-seq identifies major isoforms more robustly than short-read RNA-seq. The study showed that long-read-specific major isoforms had higher correlation between technologies and were confirmed by qPCR and dPCR to be the most abundant, while short-read-specific major isoforms were often lowly expressed and impacted by read fragmentation.
